title: Peasant Movements Bardoli Movement
definition: A landmark non-tax campaign (Satyagraha) launched in 1928 in the Bardoli taluka of Gujarat against the British colonial government's arbitrary 30% hike in land revenue.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the zenith of Gandhian mass mobilization techniques, the emergence of Sardar Patel as a national leader, and a template for successful non-violent agrarian resistance.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Peasant Movements Bardoli Movement.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
